correspondence.finding: The selected southern opening occupies a small sinuous blue channel in the delta network. The channel continues north-northeast through the flat delta plain. Both successive original parts follow the same north-northeast small-channel corridor through the delta network to the approach of the broader northward receiving reach. Generalized bends differ from individual modeled steps, but the actual published channel connection is continuous. The component name remains unverified.

The central and lower selected corridor aligns with the widening northward blue channel directly labeled Caño Cocuina on the original chart. All four short successive parts and their joins remain within that connected channel setting. A separately drawn western branch also bears Cocuina, while Caño Macareo is a distinct channel farther east.

The receiving channel continues north and bends northwest as the selected part approaches the coast. The river-to-coastal-approach linkage is visible without substituting the neighboring eastern Macareo corridor.

The two original parts follow the conspicuous westward turn into the small coastal opening and its junction setting. The larger western branch and the looping coastal shore are separately visible. No exact naming boundary or tidal-flow direction is inferred.

The last original part reaches the charted narrow opening into coastal receiving water. The source endpoint and slightly northeastern render endpoint were separately located within the same generalized mouth/coastal transition; the stored final position is retained separately. The route continues north through the broad ice passage toward the head of Independence Fjord, between the large western exposed-rock mass and eastern Mylius-Erichsen Land setting. The next three parts continue north through the widening alluvial valley with visible sinuous river reaches, gravelly margins and flat low ground. Cut-off bends and small canopy/cloud gaps do not interrupt the connected valley corridor.
